current_p1_ru: Big Baby Tape, фонк-волна (Kordhell, ICEGERGERT), Macan, Моргенштерн — русская сторона современной агрессивной музыки. Ты в центре жанра, который в РФ выстрелил мощнее, чем где-либо ещё.
current_p1_en:
Big Baby Tape, the phonk wave (Kordhell, ICEGERGERT), Macan, Morgenshtern — the Russian side of modern aggressive music. You're in the middle of a genre that exploded more powerfully in Russia than anywhere else.
This works because Russian trap and phonk aren't a copy of Western. They have their own intonation, their own slang, their own delivery. You hear this specificity and value it.
People don't always share it: "that's just noise". Not noise. It's a scene with history that began only 5 years ago and produced several bright names in that time. You caught everything from the very start.
What's worth knowing: young scenes commercialize quickly. What was fresh in 2020, by 2025 is already mass-copied. Learn to track which artists keep authenticity. Otherwise in a couple of years you'll find yourself in an imitative wave that's loud but says nothing new.

current_p1_ru: BTS, BLACKPINK, NewJeans — K-pop в твоём плейлисте. Это не «увлечение подросткой» — для тебя это ещё одна полноценная сцена, такая же серьёзная, как любая западная.
current_p1_en:
BTS, BLACKPINK, NewJeans — K-pop in your playlist. This isn't "a teenage hobby" — for you it's another full scene, just as serious as any Western one.
This works because K-pop now is one of the most diverse scenes in the world. Inside it there's everything: stadium power of BTS, conceptual explosion of aespa, retro vibe of NewJeans. You're not "a fan of K-pop in general", you listen to specific groups for specific things.
People sometimes tease you: "you're a Korean fan?". Yeah. So what? The same scene as the Western one, just in another language.
What's worth knowing: K-pop is an industry that works on intense cycles. Groups take off quickly, age quickly, new ones come constantly. If you don't follow updates, your playlist will age in a year. Learn to either accept this tempo and update, or pick one or two eternal groups as anchors.

current_p1_ru: Coldplay, Adele, Beyoncé, Taylor Swift — артисты, чьи концерты — это плач 70 тысяч человек одновременно. Тебе нужны артисты-катарсисты, которые могут собрать стадион в один эмоциональный взрыв.
current_p1_en:
Coldplay, Adele, Beyoncé, Taylor Swift — artists whose concerts are 70 thousand people crying simultaneously. You need artists of catharsis who can gather a stadium into one emotional explosion.
This works because you have a strong sense of the collective. Music for you isn't only personal experience; also shared. And the strongest moments are when thousands sing one line with you simultaneously.
People sometimes don't get it: "Coldplay is banal". And you know banality is exactly what unites. Because banal is shared, and shared is human. And in this is strength, not weakness.
What's worth knowing: stadium music works in the stadium. In headphones it often sounds "too much". If you only have epic in your playlist, you get used to one intensity and lose sensitivity to the subtle. Learn to alternate: epic for big moments + chamber for everyday. Otherwise everything turns to noise.

current_p1_ru: Old money, preppy, тихий минимализм. Ты хочешь, чтобы тебя считывали как обеспеченного человека, который не нуждается доказывать это логотипами. Это очень специфический сигнал — и его понимают только те, кто разбирается.
current_p1_en:
Old money, preppy, quiet minimalism. You want to be read as a wealthy person who doesn't need to prove it through logos. It's a very specific signal — and only those who understand it get it.
This works because you understand the hierarchy of visual codes. A loud brand is for those breaking through. Quiet expensiveness is for those already in place.
People sometimes don't read it right away. That's normal. Quiet expensiveness is for one's own. Not for the masses.
What's worth knowing: this aesthetic works only with quality. If you try to assemble it from mass market, it's immediately visible. Learn to invest in few but real things. Better three impeccable than thirty "as good as can be".

current_p1_ru: Darkwear, techwear, goth/alt. Чёрный, цепи, ботинки, технические ткани, sci-fi элементы. Ты одеваешься так, как будто живёшь в фильме о ближайшем будущем — и тебе с этим хорошо.
current_p1_en:
Darkwear, techwear, goth/alt. Black, chains, boots, technical fabrics, sci-fi elements. You dress as if you live in a film about the near future — and you're good with it.
This works because you have visual sense at the edge of reality. You don't dress "like everyone"; you create the image of a character from your own narrative.
People sometimes shy away: "are you a non-conformist?". Not a non-conformist — a different school. Just fewer people see this school.
What's worth knowing: techno aesthetic is wonderful, but in ordinary life sometimes becomes a barrier. If you come to the office in full Rick Owens, you don't "make an impression", you cause discomfort. Learn to adapt. One strong element in an ordinary outfit works much more precisely than a total look in an unsuitable environment.

current_p1_ru: Streetwear, sport casual, athleisure. Кроссовки, худи, дорогой спорт. Ты одеваешься так, как будто в любой момент можешь побежать — и тебе нравится этот вайб готовности.
current_p1_en:
Streetwear, sport casual, athleisure. Sneakers, hoodie, expensive sport. You dress as if at any moment you could run — and you like this vibe of readiness.
This works because your life rhythm requires mobility. You don't "make an impression with a suit"; you live, and clothes support you in this.
People sometimes reproach: "you're in athleisure again". Again. And I'm comfortable in it. Argument exhausted.
What's worth knowing: athleisure is a powerful genre, but requires quality. Cheap sport looks like "went to take out trash". Expensive — like a conscious choice. Learn to tell. And don't wear the same thing day after day — even in sport style there's variety.

current_p1_ru: Coquette, cottagecore, vintage thrift. Банты, кружева, цветочные принты, нежность. Ты не «модный человек» в общепринятом смысле; ты создаёшь свой пастельный мир, и одежда — его часть.
current_p1_en:
Coquette, cottagecore, vintage thrift. Bows, lace, floral prints, tenderness. You're not a "fashionable person" in the conventional sense; you create your pastel world, and clothes are part of it.
This works because you have a strong inner visual universe. Most dress "as accepted"; you — "as you feel". And this is rare.
People are sometimes surprised: "you're like a princess". Not like a princess — like a person who has inner vision. Big difference.
What's worth knowing: tender aesthetics are wonderful, but sometimes become a cage. If you don't allow yourself a single "rough" element, your style becomes one-faced. Learn to add contrast sometimes — a leather jacket over a lace dress, heavy boots under a light dress. This gives depth.

current_p1_ru: Gorpcore, techwear, athleisure. Функциональные ткани, карманы во всех местах, обувь для гор в городе. Ты одеваешься так, как будто в любой момент можешь подняться на вершину или пройти 20 км.
current_p1_en:
Gorpcore, techwear, athleisure. Functional fabrics, pockets in all places, mountain shoes in the city. You dress as if at any moment you could climb a peak or walk 20 km.
This works because you have respect for function. You don't choose clothes "beautiful" — you choose working. And in this there's also its own beauty, recognized today by the wide fashion environment.
People are sometimes surprised: "are you going hiking?". No. Just this jacket really is waterproof, and in case of rain I'll stay dry. That's the advantage.
What's worth knowing: gorpcore looks cool only in the right places. On a date in a restaurant, you in a technical jacket isn't style, it's off-key. Learn to tell situations apart. Morning in the city, in a park, on a walk — yes. At a dinner with the parents of your girlfriend/boyfriend — no.

current_p1_ru: Y2K, soft grunge, mob wife, blokecore. Тебя цепляет всё, что отсылает к нулевым и началу 2010-х. Не из ностальгии — у тебя есть глаз на то, что эпоха возвращается, и ты на её волне.
current_p1_en:
Y2K, soft grunge, mob wife, blokecore. What grabs you is everything that refers to the noughties and early 2010s. Not from nostalgia — you have an eye for the era returning, and you're on its wave.
This works because you have a sensitive feeling for cycle. Most people live in the current; you see how the old becomes new again.
People sometimes don't get it: "are those baggy jeans?". Yes, and metal glasses, and a leopard fur coat. It's all on purpose.
What's worth knowing: the return of an aesthetic works as long as irony or rethinking is preserved. If you copy the noughties literally, you're not "fashionable" — you're stuck. Learn to add modernity over the retro. Then your Y2K is style, not cosplay.

current_p1_ru: Clean girl/boy, minimal, old money, coquette. Тебя цепляет визуальная чистота. Простые палитры, ничего лишнего, ткань вместо логотипов, ухоженность вместо макияжа.
current_p1_en:
Clean girl/boy, minimal, old money, coquette. What grabs you is visual cleanness. Simple palettes, nothing extra, fabric instead of logos, groomed instead of makeup.
This works because you have a mature sense of style. You understand that cleanness is itself the highest class. Most people try to add; you — to subtract. And that is where you win.
People sometimes call it "boring": "where's the character?". Character is in quality. And it's visible if you look closely.
What's worth knowing: clean chic requires upkeep. It's an aesthetic without decor, so there's nothing to hide behind — every item is visible. Cheap fabric looks cheap, a poorly pressed shirt — wrinkled. Learn to invest in quality. Without this, clean quickly turns into 'ordinary'.

current_p1_ru: Dark academia, soft grunge, goblincore. Кожа, твид, библиотеки, мрак и осенняя меланхолия с примесью странностей. Ты живёшь в эстетике, которая отсылает к учёным комнатам и таинственным сюжетам.
current_p1_en:
Dark academia, soft grunge, goblincore. Leather, tweed, libraries, gloom and autumn melancholy with a hint of strangeness. You live in an aesthetic that refers to scholar's rooms and mysterious plots.
This works because you have deep intellectual taste. Sterile modernity bores you; you want something around with history and character.
People are sometimes surprised: "you're like from Harry Potter". Almost. And what's wrong with that?
What's worth knowing: dark academia is beautiful but requires authenticity. If books on the shelf are for beauty, not for reading, the aesthetic falls apart. If the leather on the jacket is artificial — also visible. Learn to invest in real materials. This is an aesthetic that doesn't tolerate fakery.

current_p1_ru: Cyber, acubi, maximalism. Неон, техно, балканский интернет 2024, эксперимент над эстетикой. Ты живёшь не в прошлом и не в настоящем — в будущем, которое только формируется.
current_p1_en:
Cyber, acubi, maximalism. Neon, techno, Balkan internet 2024, experiment over aesthetics. You live not in the past or in the present — in the future that's only forming.
This works because you have a nose for the new. Most catch trends a year after their peak; you — at the start.
People sometimes don't get it at all: "what kind of style is this?". And there's no such style in the mainstream yet. You're on the crest.
What's worth knowing: aesthetics on the crest are risky. If the wave doesn't reach the mainstream, you stay in your niche. Learn to combine the cutting-edge with the base — then even if the trend doesn't fire, you stay beautiful in any case.

current_p1_ru: Cottagecore, tradwife, goblincore. Ферма, пастораль, печенье, возврат к корням, лёгкая странность природы. Ты создаёшь визуальный мир, который отсылает к жизни до интернета.
current_p1_en:
Cottagecore, tradwife, goblincore. Farm, pastoral, cookies, return to roots, light strangeness of nature. You create a visual world that refers to life before the internet.
This works because you have longing for the simple. Modern life is too fast and sterile; you need something slow and warm.
People don't always share it: "you're like from the 19th century". And what's wrong with the 19th century? They had air, time, crafts. We're missing a lot of that now.
What's worth knowing: the aesthetic of returning to roots is beautiful, but sometimes becomes a form of escapism. If in 2026 you live in a visual simulation of 1850, you miss what's happening now. Learn to keep one foot in the warm past, the other in reality. Otherwise you're a tourist among your own life.

current_p1_ru: Coquette, tradwife, clean girl. Банты, пастельные цвета, нежность, ухоженность. Ты не «модный» в современном агрессивном смысле; ты создаёшь свой мягкий мир и живёшь в нём.
current_p1_en:
Coquette, tradwife, clean girl. Bows, pastel colors, tenderness, groomed. You're not "fashionable" in the modern aggressive sense; you create your soft world and live in it.
This works because you have the courage to refuse "strong" delivery in an era when everyone tries to be tough. Tenderness is your form of strength, and it's rare.
People sometimes call it "infantile". Not infantile — soft. Those are different things. You can be adult and tender; that's not a contradiction.
What's worth knowing: tender aesthetics are beautiful, but sometimes become a cage. If you don't allow yourself a single "strong" element, your image becomes one-faced. Learn to add contrast sometimes — and tenderness is revealed brighter.

current_p1_ru: Maximalism, acubi, mob wife, office siren. Тебе нужно, чтобы образ удивлял. Не «модный» — экспрессивный. Чтобы каждый день выглядел как живопись, а не как униформа.
current_p1_en:
Maximalism, acubi, mob wife, office siren. You need an image to surprise. Not "fashionable" — expressive. So that every day looks like a painting, not a uniform.
This works because you have an artistic gaze. You don't dress, you create a work. And every morning is a new canvas.
People sometimes get lost: "you're extra". And you're not "extra" — you're at 100%. It's a rare state, and most are afraid to approach it.
What's worth knowing: experiment works if there's taste behind it. Without it it's "strangeness". Learn to tell when you're "avant-garde" and when "strange without reason". The first is style. The second is loss of compass.

current_p1_ru: Дома с сериалом, ничего не делать, читать книгу, готовить ужин. Тебе нужен вечер дома — без событий, без внешнего, без обязательств.
current_p1_en:
Home with a TV show, doing nothing, reading a book, cooking dinner. You need the evening at home — without events, without external demands, without obligations.
This works because your life is intense already. The evening is a pause, a recovery point.
People sometimes invite: "come out". And you're under the blanket. And it's better there than in any bar.
What's worth knowing: home-evening is great but sometimes becomes isolation. If you're home every evening, you gradually lose social ties. Alternate — sometimes go out, even when you don't feel like it. Especially when you don't feel like it.

current_p1_ru: Тусовка с друзьями, катка с друзьями, ночной город, концерт. Тебе нужен вечер с людьми. Много, громко, ярко.
current_p1_en:
Hangout with friends, gaming with friends, the night city, a concert. You need an evening with people. Lots, loud, vivid.
This works because you have a social nature. Without people you're bored; you need to charge from shared energy.
People sometimes get tired of you: "you're calling somewhere again". Again. So what? Life is short.
What's worth knowing: social evenings exhaust, even when they seem to charge you. If you're "in people" every evening, you have no time for yourself. Alternate — an hour alone a day is needed even by the most social person.

current_p1_ru: Свидание, готовить ужин вдвоём, кинотеатр, прогулка. Тебе нужен вечер с одним важным человеком. Не группа; не одиночество — а связь.
current_p1_en:
A date, cooking dinner together, the cinema, a walk. You need an evening with one important person. Not a group; not solo — connection.
This works because you have a request for intimacy. Most people are either in a group or alone; you look for the third format — two.
People sometimes don't get it: "with him/her again?". With him/her. And every time it's like the first.
What's worth knowing: pairs are wonderful but shouldn't be the only form of leisure. If you only have "evenings with the partner", you lose both friends and yourself. Balance.

current_p1_ru: Прогулка в одиночестве, кофейня с книгой, спа, читать. Тебе нужен вечер с собой. Не одиночество как страдание; а тишина как ресурс.
current_p1_en:
A walk alone, café with a book, spa, reading. You need an evening with yourself. Not solitude as suffering; silence as resource.
This works because you have the ability to be alone. Most people run from themselves; you go toward yourself.
People sometimes don't get it: "aren't you bored?". Not bored — calm.
What's worth knowing: quiet evening is good, but sometimes becomes a habit of avoidance. If you choose "alone with a book" because you fear people — that's no longer rest, that's fear. Learn to tell.

current_p1_ru: Спортзал, прогулка, готовка, гейминг. Тебе нужно физическое движение вечером. Не «расслабиться лёжа»; а размять тело после офисного дня.
current_p1_en:
Gym, walk, cooking, gaming. You need physical motion in the evening. Not "relax lying down"; stretch the body after office day.
This works because you need physical balance. If you sat all day, the evening should be about the body.
People are sometimes surprised: "the gym after work?". The gym. And I come home more tired — but in a good way.
What's worth knowing: evening workouts can interfere with sleep. If you go to bed at 11 PM but train at 9 PM — high probability of bad sleep. Plan ahead. A workout 3+ hours before sleep — better.

current_p1_ru: Учиться чему-то новому, читать, кофейня с книгой, долгий звонок другу издалека. Тебе нужен вечер развития. Не отдых — а движение вперёд.
current_p1_en:
Learn something new, read, café with a book, long call to a friend abroad. You need an evening of development. Not rest — forward motion.
This works because you have constant curiosity. Just sitting bores you; the evening has to add something.
People sometimes don't get it: "just relax". To me this is relaxation — learning something new.
What's worth knowing: chronic learning mode exhausts. The brain also needs rest, not only new data. Learn to tell "I'm curious" from "I can't stop". The first is healthy. The second is anxiety in a mask.

current_p1_ru: Кинотеатр, концерт, кофейня, ночной город. Тебе нужен вечер впечатлений. Не «заходить покушать»; а ритуал — в правильном месте, с правильным фоном.
current_p1_en:
Cinema, concert, café, night city. You need an evening of impressions. Not "grab something to eat"; a ritual — in the right place, with the right backdrop.
This works because you have aesthetic sensitivity. Just "spending time" isn't enough; it has to be beautiful.
People sometimes don't tell them apart: "what's the difference what café". Huge. A café isn't a "place to eat", it's atmosphere.
What's worth knowing: aesthetic outings are also an investment. Good cinema, good place, good company — all costs. You're not paying for "time", you're paying for "quality of experience".

current_p1_ru: Стартап, своё дело, фриланс, блогинг. Ты не для большой корпорации. Тебе нужен риск, скорость, рост. Стабильность для тебя — это смерть мотивации.
current_p1_en:
Startup, own business, freelance, blogging. Big corporations are not your natural habitat. You need risk, speed, growth. For you, too much stability kills motivation.
This fits because you have an appetite for uncertainty. Most people fear it; you draw energy from it.
Some people worry: "and if the startup fails?". Maybe it will. Then you launch the next one. In your head it is a game, not a tragedy.
What's worth knowing: startup mode exhausts. After 5-10 years many burn out. Learn to plan recovery. And remember: 95% of startups fail. Without a financial cushion for those years you'll be forced into a corporate job at the worst possible moment.

current_p1_ru: Корпорация, госсектор, финансы, маркетинг. Тебе нужна стабильность. Большая организация, чёткие процессы, предсказуемый карьерный путь.
current_p1_en:
Corporation, public sector, finance, marketing. You need stability. A big organization, clear processes, predictable career path.
Why it works: you have an understanding of the value of durability. Most young people now rush to startups; you understand that in the long game, stability can matter more.
You may hear people say: "working in government is boring". Maybe boring. Also calm. The mortgage gets paid, the kids are okay, and your nervous system survives.
What's worth knowing: corporate stability works as long as you grow within it. If you're stuck in one role for years, stability turns into a trap. Set yourself a horizon: every 3-5 years either move up, or move out.

current_p1_ru: Дизайн, креативные индустрии, блогинг, фриланс. Ты в творческой профессии. Не «производишь продукт»; а создаёшь смысл, образ, бренд.
current_p1_en:
Design, creative industries, blogging, freelance. You belong in creative work. Not just producing a product, but creating meaning, image, brand.
It lands because you have an artistic nature. Strict number-work bores you; you need an idea behind the result.
People sometimes are surprised: "where's the stable income?". It can come. Just by a different route.
What's worth knowing: creative industries are wave-like. Sometimes orders flow, sometimes empty. Learn to plan finances around the waves. And don't confuse "creative" with "irregular" — the best creatives are disciplined.

current_p1_ru: IT-разработка, дизайн, стартап, наука. Ты в технологическом секторе. Это не просто работа — это эпоха, и ты в ней.
current_p1_en:
IT development, design, startup, science. You belong in tech. It is not just work — it is an era, and you are inside it.
The logic is simple: you have technical thinking. Most people fear code; you feel at home with it.
Some people envy IT salaries. You understand the work is also different — constant learning, new frameworks, no stability in the technologies themselves.
What's worth knowing: IT is high return but also high burnout risk. Every 2-3 years you have to retrain or you become outdated. Accept this as part of the industry. And take care of your nervous system — impostor syndrome is the occupational disease here.

current_p1_ru: Госсектор, медицина, преподавание, спорт-тренерство. Тебе нужно, чтобы работа имела смысл за пределами зарплаты. Помогать, лечить, учить — это твой формат.
current_p1_en:
Public sector, medicine, teaching, sports coaching: these make sense to you. You need work to have meaning beyond the salary. To help, heal, teach — that's your format.
This fits because you have deep motivation. Money is nice but not the main thing; what matters is what you did in someone's life.
You may hear people don't get it: "working in government for that money?". For that money, yes. And for the feeling that going to work in the morning matters.
What's worth knowing: "helping" professions often come with emotional burnout. Teachers, doctors, therapists — all on the edge. Learn to protect yourself. Without your own resources you can't help others.

current_p1_ru: Свой бизнес, фриланс, блогинг, странный креативный путь. Ты не для офиса. Тебе нужно работать на себя, по своим правилам, в своём темпе.
current_p1_en:
Own business, freelance, blogging, an unusual creative path. You're not for the office. You need work to be yours: your rules, your pace, your responsibility.
Why it works: you have independence. Submitting to others' rules is hard for you; with your own you can self-discipline.
People sometimes don't believe: "just go to an office like everyone". You are not like everyone. And you do have your own path.
What's worth knowing: "own thing" means "everything on you". Accounting, marketing, sales, product — all you. If you're not ready for that volume, you'll quit. Learn to delegate as soon as you can afford to.

current_p1_ru: Финансы, маркетинг, наука, IT-разработка. Тебе нужны числа. Анализ, отчёты, паттерны — это твоя стихия.
current_p1_en:
Finance, marketing, science, IT development. You need numbers. Analysis, reports, patterns — your element.
It lands because you have an analytical mind. Most people don't want to dig into numbers; you feel at home with them.
Some people call this "nerdy". Not nerdy — precise. And it's well paid.
What's worth knowing: analytical professions sometimes pull you away from real people. If your whole day is Excel and graphs, you gradually lose emotional communication skills. Balance — after work, real people, not more spreadsheets.

current_p1_ru: Странный креативный путь, креативные индустрии, блогинг, фриланс. Ты не вписываешься в стандартные графы. Твоя профессия — это «то, что я делаю», и она пока не имеет красивого названия.
current_p1_en:
An unusual creative path, creative industries, blogging, freelance. You don't fit standard boxes. Your profession is "what you do," and it doesn't yet have a clean name.
The logic is simple: you have the courage to go where others don't. Most people pick from ready options; you create your own.
You may hear people can't explain to their parents what you do. That's normal. In 5 years your "strange profession" might be mainstream.
What's worth knowing: "your own path" is also loneliness. You don't have "colleagues in the field" in the usual sense. Learn to find people in similar situations — even from different fields. The peer group matters even when you're a pioneer.
